prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: experimental dense facial-expression atlas for an offline GitHub Pages renderer
Primary request: transform the supplied project-owned fictional 3×3 portrait atlas into an exact 5×5 atlas of the same fictional person, adding real intermediate expression keyframes rather than duplicated or cross-faded cells.
Input image: edit target and identity/expression reference.
Composition: exactly 25 equal square cells in 5 columns and 5 rows, edge-to-edge, no margins, no labels, no grid lines. Every cell shows the same person centered at the same scale, straight-on head pose, eyes looking at camera, identical crop, hairstyle, wardrobe edge, black background, camera, white balance, and soft low-specular lighting.
Expression axes: valence increases smoothly from strongly negative at the left to strongly positive at the right. Arousal is high in the top row and decreases smoothly to low in the bottom row. Middle cell is neutral. Neighboring cells must differ only slightly. Preserve the nine supplied anchor expressions at grid positions rows 1/3/5 and columns 1/3/5 as closely as possible, and author the sixteen in-between positions consistently.
Style: natural high-detail portrait photography with realistic skin texture, friendly natural eye color and white sclera, restrained expressions, no uncanny exaggeration.
Constraints: preserve one exact identity across all 25 cells; keep facial proportions, hair strands, mole placement, shoulders, head size, background, lighting, and exposure invariant. Exactly five rows and five columns. No text, symbols, borders, seams, extra people, accessories, bloodshot eyes, glossy plastic skin, hard reflections, teeth artifacts, or watermark.

affectEvidence.layoutLesson: Use a five-valence by five-arousal authoring design.

supports: a newly generated project-owned 25-frame sheet spanning the 5x5 target positions
sixteen additional intermediate target positions relative to the 3x3 reference
offline comparison with the existing nine-anchor atlas
doesNotSupport: byte preservation of the nine reference-position cells
perceived valence or arousal validity of any generated frame
